speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information what is the rationale for the obligations placed on digital advertising intermediaries and Internet intermediaries under the Code of Practice for Transparency of Online Political Advertisements issued by the POFMA Office on 2 October 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Today, digital advertising tools are used pervasively on social media platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Moreover, digital advertisements can be micro-targeted at specific groups using a variety of indicators.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We believe that Singaporeans should know, and indeed that our citizens would want to know, who is behind the political advertisements that they see online.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, let me clarify that I have no issue with public disclosure of the originator of any online advertisements and so I agree totally that the public deserves to know who is behind the advertisement.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: One, the Code of Practice is issued under POFMA which presumably means that the concern is fake news.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But would the Minister confirm really that this Code of Practice will apply to all online advertisements, whether or not the contents contain any news alleged to be fake or not?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question, if you look at the Code of Practice at 6(c), this is the part where the companies have to maintain records for viewing by the POFMA Office.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That means not for public viewing but by the POFMA Office and the details of the information include copy of the advertisement, name of the originator, the amount paid for the advertisement, description of the advertisements' intended target audience or viewers reached, number of views and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, my question is: if the advertisement has nothing fake or alleged to be fake in it, what is the interest of the POFMA Office to know these things?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And if the Member reads the POFMA Bill, she would know that there is an overarching coverage to the Bill which includes amongst other things a need to have disclosure and/or requiring disclosure in advertising because this is an important part of the way communication is conducted today.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the event that there is falsehood in the advertisement, POFMA can potentially be applied as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Then, the Member asked about under 6(c), there is a list of details that are required and why the POFMA Office needs these.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would add that the Member might want to look at practices, for example, by Facebook which today, in fact, has the same kind of disclosure requirement and they make them publicly available and they have a register on it, including almost everything that the Member just described.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, our objective is to ensure the information is captured because, if you do not spell out clearly, and then, if you want it after the fact, it may not be available which may then thwart the intent of the legislation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And in that sense, it is a good way to discover the election strategy of the political opponents of the ruling party.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But the fact of the matter is, if you think about today's, let us just take it in practical terms, today, if you want to take out political advertising through, let us say, the English social media platforms.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I am not sure how this affords us greater intelligence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: By the way, the intelligence will be available through Facebook's actions, for example.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think the Member might be barking up the wrong tree on this.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
